question.worked_solution:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=1-{x}^{2},$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(x) & =1, \\ {v}^{′}(x) & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (1-{x}^{2})-x\cdot (-2x)}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1-{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1+{x}^{2}}{{(1-{x}^{2})}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
